article_title: Simulation-based training in professional education: learning, participation, and instructional design
citation: Charlott Sellberg & Oskar Lindwall. (2025). Simulation-based training in professional education: learning, participation, and instructional design. Instructional Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-025-09763-2
title: The briefing–scenario–debriefing (BSD) cycle as a design scaffold for distributing guidance, feedback, and representational work over time
description: The editorial describes the briefing–scenario–debriefing cycle as a widely used framework for structuring simulation instruction: a prospective phase prepares learners, an in-action phase supports performance, and a retrospective phase renders experience accountable and generalisable. Conceptually, "the BSD cycle is less a fixed script than a design scaffold for distributing guidance, feedback, and representational work over time". Briefings translate curriculum goals into attentional priorities; debriefings convert concrete experiences into general principles.
requirements: Briefings must translate curriculum goals into attentional priorities and familiarise learners with the simulation environment; debriefings must convert experiences into generalisable insights
constraints: The BSD cycle is only one of many ways to embed simulations within broader instructional designs
target_learning_goals: converting simulation experience into general principles and actionable insights
examples: Nursing debriefings use annotated timelines, clipped video, or live-captured notes; military post-wargame debriefings use maps, gestures, and narrated fragments of play
key_sources: Charlott Sellberg & Oskar Lindwall. (2025). Simulation-based training in professional education: learning, participation, and instructional design. Instructional Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-025-09763-2

article_title: Using blended synchronous classroom approach to promote learning performance in rural area
citation: Yang, J; Yu, H; Chen, NS. (2019). Using blended synchronous classroom approach to promote learning performance in rural area. Computers and Education. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2019.103619
title: BSC synchronous technology configuration (video conferencing, electronic whiteboards, interactive response systems)
description: The technology configuration through which BSC integrates classrooms: "various synchronous tools such as video conferencing systems, electronic whiteboards, interactive response systems". These tools connect urban and rural physical classrooms with synchronous cyber classrooms and asynchronous cyber classrooms to support online real-time interaction. The element was deployed in the two-year Ningbo project.
requirements: Internet technology infrastructure connecting physically separate classrooms
target_learners: Primary school students in rural and urban schools
target_learning_goals: Real-time interaction between remote and local classrooms during instruction
examples: Used to fully integrate two or more physical classrooms in the two-year BSC project in two primary schools
key_sources: Yang, J; Yu, H; Chen, NS. (2019). Using blended synchronous classroom approach to promote learning performance in rural area. Computers and Education. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2019.103619

article_title: Training Individuals to Implement Discrete Trials with Fidelity: A Meta-Analysis
citation: Joelle Fingerhut and Mariola Moeyaert. (2022). Training Individuals to Implement Discrete Trials with Fidelity: A Meta-Analysis. Focus on Autism and Other Developmental Disabilities. https://doi.org/10.1177/10883576221081076
title: Behavioral skills training as a four-component training package
description: Behavioral skills training (BST) is a training package that "includes the four training methods of feedback, instruction, modeling, and rehearsal delivered together and/or sequentially." The article defines each component operationally: feedback is performance feedback from an observer, instruction is verbal, digital, or print information, modeling is a live or video demonstration, and rehearsal is structured role-play with a trainer in the presence of a trainer. The meta-analysis uses these dummy-coded components as moderators of DTT implementation fidelity gains.
requirements: For the meta-analysis definition, BST occurred when instruction, modeling, rehearsal, and feedback were implemented simultaneously or sequentially during the training
constraints: Instruction could not be isolated as a variable because 96% of studies included it; feedback could not be isolated because only 11% of studies included it separate from BST
target_learning_goals: accurate implementation of discrete trial training with fidelity
examples: In the meta-analysis, 130 (58%) of 224 participants received BST as their training, and BST recipients reached 96.06% average implementation fidelity
key_sources: Joelle Fingerhut and Mariola Moeyaert. (2022). Training Individuals to Implement Discrete Trials with Fidelity: A Meta-Analysis. Focus on Autism and Other Developmental Disabilities. https://doi.org/10.1177/10883576221081076

article_title: Effects of the 5E Instructional Model: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
citation: Polanin, J. R., Austin, M., Taylor, J. A., Steingut, R. R., Rodgers, M. A., & Williams, R. (2024). Effects of the 5E Instructional Model: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. AERA Open. https://doi.org/10.1177/23328584241269866
title: The BSCS 5E Instructional Model and its 3E and 7E variants
description: The BSCS 5E Instructional Model is a constructivist framework for organizing and sequencing science instruction through five stages—engagement, exploration, explanation, elaboration, and evaluation—in which "the teacher serves as a facilitator, guiding students through each 'E' stage of the learning process". The 3E variant retains only explore, explain, and elaborate, while the 7E variant adds elicit and extend stages to make evocation of prior conceptions and far transfer more explicit. All three build on constructivist learning theory and incorporate the How People Learn findings on engaging prior knowledge and metacognition.
requirements: Requires a curricular enactment of at least five class periods or 4 hours, not a single 5E lesson, per the review's eligibility definition
constraints: The 3E model lacks an overt engage/elicit stage and an evaluation stage, which the authors hypothesize explains its smaller effects
target_learners: pre-K through grade 12 students in school-based STEM settings
examples: The review included 61 RCTs of curricular enactments: 45 studies of the 5E model (74%) and 8 studies each of the 3E and 7E models (13% each), with an average implementation duration of 7.7 weeks
key_sources: Polanin, J. R., Austin, M., Taylor, J. A., Steingut, R. R., Rodgers, M. A., & Williams, R. (2024). Effects of the 5E Instructional Model: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. AERA Open. https://doi.org/10.1177/23328584241269866

article_title: Effects of Concept Mapping Instruction Approach on Students' Achievement in Basic Science
citation: Ukpai Patricia Ogonnaya, Gabriel Okafor, Okechukwu S. Abonyi, J.O Ugama. (2016). Effects of Concept Mapping Instruction Approach on Students’ Achievement in Basic Science. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.7, No.8. https://www.iiste.org
title: Basic Science Achievement Test (BSAT), a 30-item multiple-choice instrument
description: The researchers developed the Basic Science Achievement Test (BSAT) as "a 30 item multiple choice test" built from the content covered in the study, with items drawn using a table of specification. It covered three topics in the lesson note plan: the living components of the environment, grouping of living things, and classification of living things. The instrument was subjected to face and content validation, and its Kuder Richardson coefficient of internal consistency is 0.97.
requirements: Face and content validation and a table of specification for item construction, as the article reports
constraints: Covers only the three topics taught in the study's lesson note plan
target_learners: JSS I junior secondary school students
target_learning_goals: measuring achievement in basic science topics
examples: Pretest and posttest administrations of the BSAT supplied the covariate and outcome data for the ANCOVA analyses.
key_sources: Ukpai Patricia Ogonnaya, Gabriel Okafor, Okechukwu S. Abonyi, J.O Ugama. (2016). Effects of Concept Mapping Instruction Approach on Students’ Achievement in Basic Science. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.7, No.8. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1095361

article_title: Concept Mapping Strategy: An Effective Tool for Improving Students' Academic Achievement in Biology
citation: Sakiyo, J. & Waziri, K. (2015). Concept mapping strategy: An effective tool for improving students' academic achievement in biology. Journal of Education in Science, Environment and Health (JESEH), 1(1), 56-62. www.jeseh.net
title: Biology Students' Achievement Test (BSAT)
description: The Biology Students' Achievement Test (BSAT) is the 60-item four-option multiple-choice achievement instrument used to measure outcomes, adapted from West African Examination Council biology tests from 2005 to 2010. Items span six cognitive domains of educational objectives, with Knowledge and Comprehension at 25% each, Application and Analysis at 15% each, and Synthesis and Evaluation at 10% each. It was content validated by three experts, pilot tested on 30 students from a non-participating school, and "yielded a Cronbach alpha reliability index of 0.78".
requirements: Content validation by three experts and pilot testing were part of its development as described
constraints: Adapted specifically from WAEC biology tests 2005-2010 and administered as pre-test and post-test in this study
target_learning_goals: biology achievement across knowledge, comprehension, application, analysis, synthesis and evaluation
examples: The BSAT was administered as a pre-test in the first week and as a post-test after six weeks of instruction to both groups
key_sources: Sakiyo, J. & Waziri, K. (2015). Concept mapping strategy: An effective tool for improving students' academic achievement in biology. Journal of Education in Science, Environment and Health (JESEH), 1(1), 56-62. www.jeseh.net. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1105286

article_title: Effect of Self Regulated Learning Approach on Junior Secondary School Students' Achievement in Basic Science
citation: Nwafor Chika E, Abigail Chikaodinaka Obodo, Gabriel Okafor. (2015). Effect of Self Regulated Learning Approach on Junior Secondary School Students' Achievement in Basic Science. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.6, No.5. http://www.iiste.org
title: Basic Science Achievement Test (BSAT), a 50-item multiple-choice instrument
description: The Basic Science Achievement Test (BSAT) is "a 50-item multiple-choice test" whose items were drawn from the module Saving your Energy, with item distribution guided by a test blueprint. It was face and content validated by specialists and subjected to item analysis for difficulty and discrimination. Reliability was assessed by test-retest (stability index 0.93) and K-R 20 internal consistency (0.91). The same test served as pretest and posttest, with items reshuffled and different coloured papers to reduce memorisation effects.
requirements: Administered as both pretest and posttest with reshuffled item order to reduce errors of memorization
constraints: Items cover only the five units of the Saving your Energy module
target_learners: JSS II students in Enugu State, Nigeria
target_learning_goals: Achievement in Basic Science energy topics
examples: Used to collect pre and posttest data from two intact classes in each of two coeducational secondary schools
key_sources: Nwafor Chika E, Abigail Chikaodinaka Obodo, Gabriel Okafor. (2015). Effect of Self Regulated Learning Approach on Junior Secondary School Students' Achievement in Basic Science. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.6, No.5. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1083647

article_title: Learning Environments as Basis for Cognitive Achievements of Students in Basic Science Classrooms in Nigeria
citation: Atomatofa, R., Okoye, N., & Igwebuike, T. (2016). Learning Environments as Basis for Cognitive Achievements of Students in Basic Science Classrooms in Nigeria. Universal Journal of Educational Research 4(6): 1471-1478. https://doi.org/10.13189/ujer.2016.040627
title: BSACT and BSSAT instruments for basic science achievement and ability grouping
description: The study used two evaluation packages plus teaching guides. The Basic Science Achievement Test (BSACT) consists of 40 objective questions drawn from past junior certificate exam questions of the Delta State Ministry of Education, administered as pretest and re-arranged as posttest; its Kuder-Richardson 21 reliability coefficient was 0.82 in a pilot on 30 students. The Basic Science Scholastic Ability Test (BSSAT) consists of 30 questions from Junior Secondary one term exams, used to categorize students into high and low ability; its KR-21 coefficient was 0.70.
requirements: Instruments were subjected to face validity by two measurement and evaluation experts and a senior basic science teacher, with a table of specification for BSACT content validity
constraints: The middle ability band (40-59%) was excluded from hypothesis two testing
target_learners: junior secondary students in Delta State, Nigeria
target_learning_goals: basic science achievement and scholastic ability measurement
examples: The BSSAT was administered two weeks before treatment and results were collected the same day to categorize students into high and low ability
key_sources: Atomatofa, R., Okoye, N., & Igwebuike, T. (2016). Learning Environments as Basis for Cognitive Achievements of Students in Basic Science Classrooms in Nigeria. Universal Journal of Educational Research 4(6): 1471-1478. https://doi.org/10.13189/ujer.2016.040627

article_title: Simulation-based training for teaching infection prevention: from realistic to virtual environments.
citation: Souza Raissa Silva; Carvalho Dárlinton Barbosa Feres; Félix Adriana Maria da Silva; Dias Ana Angélica Lima. (2025). Simulation-based training for teaching infection prevention: from realistic to virtual environments. Revista Brasileira de Enfermagem. https://doi.org/10.1590/0034-7167-2024-0288
title: 3D virtual environment simulator for teaching bloodstream infection prevention related to peripheral venous catheters
description: A computer-based simulation scenario developed on the Unity 3D platform to expand the reach of a validated hybrid realistic simulation for teaching nursing students and professionals best practices for BSI prevention related to PVCs. It models a nursing station and a patient room, a nurse avatar representing the learner and a patient avatar reporting acute pain at a saline-locked PVC. The artifact was "evaluated positively by a panel of experts", though a fully functional 3D version is not yet available.
requirements: Built from a freely available Unity 3D environment asset template, modified to comply with relevant regulations and aligned with the clinical case
constraints: A fully functional version of the artifact within the proposed three-dimensional environment is not yet available
target_learning_goals: Best practices for bloodstream infection prevention related to peripheral venous catheters
examples: The scenario begins in a nursing station; the participant clicks to move the nurse avatar, interact with objects, and obtain the patient's complaint
key_sources: Souza Raissa Silva; Carvalho Dárlinton Barbosa Feres; Félix Adriana Maria da Silva; Dias Ana Angélica Lima. (2025). Simulation-based training for teaching infection prevention: from realistic to virtual environments. Revista Brasileira de Enfermagem. https://doi.org/10.1590/0034-7167-2024-0288

article_title: The effect of simulation-based breast health education on breast cancer awareness and breast self-examination skills of Afghan refugee women: a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Kuru Alici Nilgün, Arikan Dönmez Ayşe, Aktaş Okşan, Zeytun Zeybek. (2025). The effect of simulation-based breast health education on breast cancer awareness and breast self-examination skills of Afghan refugee women: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Public Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-025-23313-y
title: BSE Skill Assessment Form (15-item observational checklist)
description: A structured observational checklist developed by the researchers to assess practical BSE performance rather than self-reported behavior, covering 'inspection techniques, palpation coverage, positioning, and systematic approach' across 15 items. Content validity used Davis's technique with expert opinions from seven academicians; inter-rater agreement tested on five pilot-study women reached a weighted Cohen's Kappa of κ = 0.86, indicating high assessor agreement.
requirements: All raters received comprehensive training by the primary investigator before assessment; items were considered valid when the content validity index exceeded 0.80.
constraints: Skill scores rest on researcher observation of performance rather than participant self-report.
target_learners: Afghan refugee women undergoing practical BSE skill evaluation
target_learning_goals: Objective assessment of practical breast self-examination performance
examples: In the trial the form was completed by a data-collecting researcher who was unaware of participants' group assignments, supporting assessor blinding.
key_sources: Kuru Alici Nilgün, Arikan Dönmez Ayşe, Aktaş Okşan, Zeytun Zeybek. (2025). The effect of simulation-based breast health education on breast cancer awareness and breast self-examination skills of Afghan refugee women: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Public Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-025-23313-y
